newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu warns Arafat against declaring state.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu warns Arafat against declaring state.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday said any unilateral Palestinian declaration of an independent state would violate peace deals and that he had a plan ready should the PLO take such a step.

Netanyahu also said during an interview with Israel's Channel One television that he would make it a condition of implementation of interim peace deals with the Palestine Liberation Organisation that the PLO should observe its side of the accords.
"The (interim) agreements do not prevent the Palestinians from raising for the permanent settlement their proposal of a Palestinian state which we oppose," Netanyahu said.

"But they certainly cannot do that unilaterally because that is a violation of the agreement. And if there will be a violation of the agreement like that...that is to say one that is a fundamental violation of the agreement, then the principle of reciprocity operates with all its force."
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in Cairo on Wednesday that he would eventually declare a Palestinian state despite opposition from Israel.

Asked what Israel could do against such a move by Arafat, Netanyahu said: "A lot, a lot. Believe me, I have a plan ready in the drawer...I'm convinced he understands this. It is possible to say a lot of things."
The Israeli pullback from most of the West Bank town of Hebron last week after months of acrimonious negotiations has revived Israel's peace moves with the PLO.
The Hebron deal included "reciprocal agreements" in which both sides committed themselves to carrying out mutual undertakings in previous peace deals.
